title: Preservation of classical Koszul cohomology under support and pullback
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its norm-topological valuation ring $B$, and the sectionwise uniformizer scalar $\pi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, det-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution]. Let $p$ be a path from a vertex $S$ to the root $X$ of a finite qcqs open-closed tree [def-sfb-qcqs-open-closed-tree]. Write $J$ for its actual module functor, using open extension by zero and closed direct image at each edge, and identity for the root [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek, def-sfb-module-lower-star]. For an arbitrary internal $B_S$-module $I$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and $n\in\mathbf N$ form $C_n(I)=[I\xrightarrow{\pi^n}I]$ in degrees $-1,0$. Suppose every abelian $H^q C_n(I)$ is in the essential image of $\nu_S^*$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Then for every scheme morphism $v:U\to X$ [def-pc-scheme] and every integer $q$, $H^q C_n(v^*J(I))$ is in the essential image of $\nu_U^*$, using the actual internal-module pullback [def-sfb-module-upper-star]. No Noetherian, constructibility, or finite-local-model hypothesis is imposed; this is a preservation statement with classicality as input. Empty paths and $n=0$ are allowed.

proof.text: For each integer q choose an abelian etale antecedent F_q for the classical sheaf H^q C_n(I), using the hypothesis. Induct along the support path. The root is the identity. At an open branch, extension by zero is exact and commutes with comparison inverse image. At a closed branch, the immersion is qcqs: affine inverse images are quotient spectra, and its diagonal is an isomorphism. The degree-zero clause of direct-image comparison, applied to F_q[0], gives comparison compatibility for ordinary direct image. Its pro-etale direct image is exact because the complementary open immersion is quasi-compact, as required by the tree. Internal-module operations transport identifies these underlying abelian functors and their scalar actions. Thus induction gives a classical antecedent for J H^q C_n(I), in every degree. The argument is abelian-valued (equivalently uses discrete integer coefficients), and requires no finite quotient action on F_q.

source.place: Tag 09BN lemma-open-immersion; Tag 09BM lemma-closed-immersion-complement-retrocompact-exact; Tag 09A6 lemma-morphism-comparison and open-extension comparison.

proof.text: Module pullback along v is exact and transports to the underlying sheaf inverse image with its pulled-back coefficient action. Its comparison square identifies v^* nu_X^* F with nu_U^* v_et^* F for every abelian etale sheaf F, without any qcqs assumption on v. Since all the support and pullback functors are additive and linear, they take multiplication by the specified resolution scalar to the same scalar. Exact-functor cohomology therefore identifies H^q C_n(v^* J I) with v^* J H^q C_n(I). The antecedents from the path induction and the inverse-image square prove the conclusion in each q. This includes n=0, root paths, zero objects and empty schemes.

source.place: Tag 09A5 section-morphism, inverse-image comparison square; exactness and cohomology transported through the cited module equivalences.

theorem support_pullback_koszul_classical
    (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra (Padic ℓ) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic ℓ) E]
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} {tree : QcqsOpenClosedTree X} (p : tree.Path S)
    (I : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology S) Ab.{u + 1})
      (condensedRingObj (DerivedNakayama.integerRing ℓ E) S))
    (n : ℕ)
    (hI : ∀ q : ℤ, (comparisonUpperStar Ab.{u + 1} S).essImage
      ((HomologicalComplex.double
        (((DerivedNakayama.scalarOnModules ℓ E S
          ((DerivedNakayama.derived_nakayama_resolution ℓ E).choose ^ n)).app
            I).hom) (c := ComplexShape.up ℤ) (i₀ := -1) (i₁ := 0) (by decide)).homology q))
    {U : Scheme.{u}} (v : U ⟶ X) :
    ∀ q : ℤ, (comparisonUpperStar Ab.{u + 1} U).essImage
      ((HomologicalComplex.double
        (((DerivedNakayama.scalarOnModules ℓ E U
          ((DerivedNakayama.derived_nakayama_resolution ℓ E).choose ^ n)).app
            ((CondensedRing.upperStar (DerivedNakayama.integerRing ℓ E) v).obj
              ((p.extension (DerivedNakayama.integerRing ℓ E)).obj I))).hom)
        (c := ComplexShape.up ℤ) (i₀ := -1) (i₁ := 0)
        (by decide)).homology q)
